src: APSLPRB SI Prelims Paper-I 2023
s: In August 2022 Supreme Court declared that Section 3(2) of the Benami Transactions (Prohibition) Act 1988 as unconstitutional. Section 3(2) of this act gives provision of the following punishment.
o: Three years maximum imprisonment or fine or both.
Properties held benami shall be subject to confiscation by Authority.
Maximum 5 years imprisonment and confiscation of properties.
x:
the Aug 2022 Ganpati Dealcom judgment striking down Sec 3(2) was recalled in Oct 2024 on the Union's review petition — now the declaration of unconstitutionality no longer stands (taxmann.com).
Section 3 of the original Benami Transactions (Prohibition) Act, 1988 made entering into a benami transaction punishable with up to three years' imprisonment, or fine, or both; in Ganpati Dealcom (23 Aug 2022) the SC held it unconstitutional (that ruling was recalled in Oct 2024, so it is not unconstitutional now). Confiscation and 1-7 years' RI come from the 2016 amendment, not Sec 3(2) of 1988.

src: APPSC Group-1 PYQ
s:
Consider the following statements with reference to the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002:
I. The Act empowers authorities like the Director to attach property believed to be " proceeds of crime ".
II. Offences under Part A of the Schedule deal with trans-border crimes and reflect the dedication to tackle money laundering across the global boundaries.
III. The Act and the Rules notified thereunder came into force with effect from 2005.
IV. The Act has provided for an Appellate Tribunal and Special Court to conduct the trial of the offences of money laundering.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: I, III and IV are correct: the ED Director can attach proceeds of crime, the Act and Rules came into force on 1 July 2005, and the Act provides an Appellate Tribunal and Special Courts. II is wrong: offences with cross-border implications are Part C of the Schedule, not Part A.

src: APPSC AEE Mains General Studies & Mental Ability 2016
s: Definition of "proceeds of crime" in Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002 was amended in
x: The Finance Act, 2015 (w.e.f. 14 May 2015) amended the PMLA definition of 'proceeds of crime' to cover property taken or held outside the country (equivalent value within India). It was widened again in 2018 and 2019, after this 2016 exam.

src: UPSC Civils Prelims 2019
s:
Consider the following statements:

A. The United Nations Convention against Corruption (UNCAC) has a 'Protocol against the Smuggling of Migrants by Land, Sea and Air'.

B. The UNCAC is the ever-first legally binding global anti-corruption instrument.

C. A highlight of the United Nations Convention against Transnational Organized Crime (UNTOC) is the inclusion of a specific chapter aimed at returning assets to their rightful owners from whom they had been taken illicitly.

D. The United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC) is mandated by its member States to assist in the implementation of both UNCAC and UNTOC.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: B and D are correct: UNCAC is the only legally binding universal anti-corruption instrument, and UNODC assists in implementing both UNCAC and UNTOC. A is wrong (the smuggling-of-migrants protocol belongs to UNTOC) and C is wrong (the asset-recovery chapter, Chapter V, is in UNCAC, not UNTOC).

src: UPSC CSE Prelims 1998
s: Capital Account Convertibility of the Indian Rupee implies
o: that the Indian Rupee can be exchanged by the authorised dealers for travel
that the Indian Rupee can be exchanged for any major currency for the purpose of trade in goods and
that the Indian Rupee can be exchanged for any major currency for the purpose of trading financial assets
x: Capital account convertibility means the rupee can be freely exchanged for any major currency to trade financial assets (investment, loans); exchange for trade in goods and services is current account convertibility.
